sections.label: NS deferment criteria for sportsmen
sections.summary: Questions ask what criteria determine sportsman NS deferment, whether different criteria apply to hard-to-measure sports, and to individual versus team sportsmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Defence (a) what are the criteria that are used to determine whether a sportsman can be deferred from National Service to pursue his sporting growth and development; (b) whether there are different criteria used to assess the potential of sportsmen who are taking part in sports where success is not easily measured using quantitative benchmarks; and (c) whether there are different criteria used for individual sportsmen and those participating in team sports and, if so, what are the criteria used for individuals participating in team sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Defence whether the Government can consider deferring National Service for outstanding young male Singaporeans who have the potential to accomplish significant successes in fields other than sports if those successful achievements can also bring international fame and recognition for Singapore.

sections.label: Team sports deferment and review
sections.summary: Questions ask whether team sports deferments are considered, what evidence is required, what consultation occurs, what cases are exceptional, and when policy is reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Defence (a) whether National Service deferments can be considered for team sports and not only for individual sports; (b) what documents and supporting evidence are required to meet the criteria for deferment; (c) what consultation is held with direct and supporting parties in evaluating deferment applications; (d) what types of cases does the Ministry deem to be exceptional; and (e) when was the deferment policy last reviewed and when will it be next reviewed.

sections.label: NS defaulters prosecuted
sections.summary: Refusing to serve NS when required and returning at one's own choosing strikes at national security, universality and equity; thirteen defaulters were prosecuted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: When a person refuses to serve NS at the time that he is required to and instead returns to serve at a time of his own choosing, or worse, at an age when he can no longer serve, his actions strike at the very core of the principles of national security, universality and equity." Thirteen NS defaulters were prosecuted after the new sentencing framework was established last year.

sections.label: Courts dismiss personal reasons
sections.summary: Courts dismissed personal reasons such as supporting families, convicting and jailing offenders because the Enlistment Act is blind to personal convenience and considerations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Others said they had to support their families.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But in every case, in every judgment, the Courts dismissed these personal reasons, convicted and sentenced them to jail because, harsh as it is, the Enlistment Act is blind to "personal convenience and considerations", no matter how talented the individual, no matter how exceptional his circumstances.

sections.label: Selective deferment for Singapore's interest
sections.summary: MINDEF will defer individuals very selectively only if deferment serves Singapore's interest first, the basis for deferring three sportsmen for Olympics training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Mr Suresh Nair, who wrote to our feedback unit and said this, "Let this Davis case be the right and timely reminder of the need for absolute fairness in applying laws regarding NS deferment".

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Therefore, to preserve equity for all National Servicemen, MINDEF will only defer individuals very selectively if their deferment serves Singapore's interest first and foremost, never their own.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This was the only basis to defer three sportsmen, swimmers Joseph Schooling and Quah Zheng Wen, and sailor Maximilian Soh, from NS so that they could train and compete in the Olympics.

sections.label: Ben Davis and Harvey Davis
sections.summary: Ben Davis plays for Fulham FC as an English national, not a Singaporean citizen, and Harvey Davis refused to indicate when his son would return to serve NS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: First, Mr Ben Davis is playing for Fulham FC as an English national, not a Singaporean Citizen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Second, Mr Harvey Davis has consistently refused to indicate when his son would return to serve NS, if deferred.

sections.label: Father considered citizenship renunciation
sections.summary: After MINDEF rejected the application, Mr Harvey Davis said he would consider his son renouncing Singapore citizenship to pursue his career.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In fact, Mr Harvey Davis went further after MINDEF rejected the application – that he would consider the option for his son to renounce his Singapore citizenship in order to pursue his career.

sections.label: MINDEF rejects deferment application
sections.summary: MINDEF could not find any valid grounds to approve Mr Harvey Davis's application for deferment for his son.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: MINDEF could not find any valid grounds to approve the application for deferment by Mr Harvey Davis for his son.

sections.label: Three other talent-spotted footballers
sections.summary: To MINDEF's knowledge, three other footballers have also been talent-spotted to take part in trials for professional leagues overseas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: To MINDEF's knowledge, there are three other footballers who have also been talent-spotted to take part in trials for professional leagues overseas.

sections.label: Footballers' overseas club trials
sections.summary: Irfan and Ikhsan play for the Young Lions and represent Singapore, and Irfan, Saifullah and Ikhsan are slated for trials at European clubs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Irfan and Ikhsan are now playing for the Young Lions in the Singapore Premier League and representing Singapore in regional football competitions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I understand Irfan has gone for trials with European clubs, including an upcoming trial with Sporting Braga, and Saifullah and Ikhsan are slated to follow suit at CD Tenerife and Braga.

sections.label: Asian Games National Servicemen postponement
sections.summary: For the upcoming Asian Games, 10 National Servicemen have been given short postponements of enlistment or time off to train.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For the upcoming Asian Games later this month, so far, 10 of our National Servicemen have been given a short postponement of their enlistment of a few weeks, or if they have been enlisted, they have been given time off to train for the Games.

sections.label: MINDEF working with sports agencies
sections.summary: MINDEF will work with MCCY, SportSG and other agencies through pathways letting sportsmen do well and still fulfil National Service obligations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: MINDEF will work with MCCY, SportSG and other relevant agencies through various pathways that can allow sportsmen to do well and still fulfil their National Service obligations, whether it is individual or team sports.

sections.label: Courts uphold sentencing benchmarks
sections.summary: The Courts have upheld the sentencing benchmarks, and after their revision, 13 defaulters went to jail.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We have to understand that our Courts have upheld it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I said, after the revision of the sentencing benchmarks, 13 defaulters went to jail.

sections.label: Long-term deferments for sportsmen
sections.summary: Over 15 years, long-term deferments were agreed for three sportsmen who met the standards, to be fair to other National Servicemen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In the last 15 years, we have agreed to long-term deferments for three sportsmen who met that, and we will continue to keep to those standards so that we can be fair to other National Servicemen who do their NS dutifully, who put aside their own careers to do NS, as well as not undermine the Court's basis for sentencing those who default their National Service.

sections.label: Deferment criteria and examples
sections.summary: Deferment is possible if it maintains equity for National Servicemen and serves national interest, never personal interest; exceptional musicians have been deferred.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The answer is yes, if it satisfies the criteria that I talked about, that we maintain equity for all other National Servicemen, and that it serves the national interest, never their own.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The first example the Member gave was that he competes in tennis and then he decides he wants to be a professional tennis player before he comes back, obviously, that will affect our considerations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We have gone on record to say that we have deferred some very exceptional musicians.

sections.label: 2012 Minister reply on athletes
sections.summary: The 2012 Minister reply stated 13 athletes were deferred for two to six months for the 2011 SEA Games and 2010 Asian Games.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the 2012 reply given by the Minister, it was stated that 13 athletes were deferred for a period of two to six months to participate in the 2011 SEA Games and the 2010 Asian Games.

sections.label: No change in deferment policy
sections.summary: Hansard records no change in deferment policy, which must maintain equity for all National Servicemen and serve national interest, never personal interest.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The Hansard says so and there is no change in our deferment policy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: On the fundamental principles, we must maintain equity for all National Servicemen, and it must be for national interest, never for personal interest.

sections.label: Doubt over returning from abroad
sections.summary: MINDEF questions how it can believe someone earning a few hundred pounds a week abroad would return to serve NS when earning much more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If you are not willing to come back to serve your NS when you are earning a few hundred pounds a week, how is MINDEF to believe that you would come back when you are earning many times more?
